title: Indexing & .at()
description: Arrays are zero-indexed; use .at() for ergonomic negative indexing from the end.

notes: arr[-1] does NOT give the last element — it returns undefined (negative is a string key, not an index).
Out-of-bounds access returns undefined silently — guard or use ?? for defaults.
.at() is ES2022; safe in modern browsers and Node 16+. Prefer it over arr[arr.length - 1].

options: getter that runs a count loop

exercises.prompt: Log the first and last element using bracket indexing.
Use .at() with negative indices to log the last two elements.

L3.prompt: Write `lastTwo(arr)` returning the last two elements as a 2-element array using .at(). Log `JSON.stringify(lastTwo([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]))`.
